How to develop a user model

This public copy explains how to develop a grounded account of the actual person for a situated Yinyang package. The account helps a counterpart understand their activity, interpret requests, and contribute fittingly. Its object is a person acting in particular situations, with purposes, capacities, experiences, and changing conditions. A collection of traits would miss how these relations affect one another. The person always exceeds the account.

Someone borrowing this method can develop only the understanding their current work needs. Full adoption uses this account alongside the other four under the formation method. Neither route requires a complete biography, clinical explanation, or personal philosophy project before useful work begins.

Understand activity in its situation

Start from relevant attributable expression and actual participation. A conversation about a difficult decision may reveal a purpose and competing concerns; a correction during implementation may reveal a mistaken division of work; an established practice may show a capacity or useful support. Selected personal writing, psychological or preference material, and philosophical expression may deepen understanding where relevant and available. Enter through the more developed material and check it against the others. An available archive is not a reason to read everything in it.

Develop the connections that explain a real difference in collaboration. What is the person trying to understand or accomplish? What do they contribute through recognition, generation, judgment, expression, and action? Which conditions support or obstruct that activity? What do they want to keep, change, or learn? These questions orient connected prose; they are not fields every person must fill. Explain supported relationships and keep an unknown relation unknown.

In a fictional example, someone readily develops an argument in conversation but finds turning it into a finished document costly. Several accounts are possible: dialogue helps ideas take shape; the editing interface is cumbersome; or this particular task has little value for them. Relevant expression and work can distinguish those possibilities. If dialogue is a useful support, the model can help structure and write while the person generates, recognizes, and revises ideas. That division establishes neither inability to write nor a reason to prefer speech in every situation.

Preserve the grounds of an interpretation

A reported experience, explanatory interpretation, chosen preference, and developmental intention support different conclusions. “This exchange felt interruptive” reports an experience. “Every interruption destroys my attention” extends its scope. A commitment to carry implementation details is a chosen response. Preserve the differences where a future counterpart could otherwise turn a local observation into a standing rule.

The same arrangement can result from preference, constraint, habit, or a default. A tool in daily use does not by itself show why the person uses it. Compare their explanation, relevant corrections, alternatives actually available, and effects in work. When the distinction would change the result and evidence cannot settle it, a focused inquiry can obtain the missing experience or purpose. The model carries interpretation and writing rather than requiring the person to deliver a finished self-description.

Preferences can supply a useful working account when psychological mechanisms are unknown. Explain what the person values, chooses, or wishes to change and under what conditions. A philosophical image can suggest a connection; coherence does not prove that connection in this life. Use psychological vocabulary at the strength the evidence permits, without turning interpretation into diagnosis or chosen support into deficit.

Let understanding change the work

Connect the account to the counterpart and relationship: what contribution follows, what remains a candidate, and what use could correct. The counterpart-and-relationship guide develops that writing duty; the encounter guide helps condense the needed whole. Use the sources-and-grounds guide to keep source identity, time, conflicting evidence, and access limits navigable. Extended episodes and personal details stay with their private owners.

Date changing conditions when time matters. Revise a claim when the person corrects it, circumstances change, or use exposes poor fit. Consider whether failure concerns understanding, the chosen relationship, or its realization before rewriting the person to fit a tool. Better task results support a practical arrangement; enduring learning or development needs evidence at that larger scale. The account serves actual life and work while remaining open to what it has not understood.
